Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Were confirming the pilot go-live for WellHealth on Monday 2028-07-17 at 10:00 AM PT. The launch team expects two ramp phases: a soft open (first 6 hours) and then a traffic spike window during business hours (12:00 PM - 4:00 PM PT). Key numbers from our simulation: peak ingress ~9,000 requests/min for ~2 hours, sustained 3,000-4,000 requests/min outside the spike. Median payload length ~1.2k tokens; many sessions include multi-message chat with short context retention.

Were attaching the traffic model (wellhealth_traffic_model_v2.csv) and a short request doc asking for a temporary rate allowance while the pilot stabilizes (temp-rate-exempt-request.pdf). Specific ask: temporary increase to 80 requests/sec (aggregated across API keys used in the pilot) for a 72-hour window starting at go-live, plus a one-time routing preference to the us-west region and pin to the 8-bit quantized variant of the model if available.

Can Redwood confirm feasibility and any product asks we should prepare for? Were happy to take a short sync today if helpful.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Launch Ops, WellHealth

Folks, forwarding WellHealth's traffic profile and temporary rate ask. High level:
- Go-live Monday 7/17 10:00 AM PT, 72-hour window for temp allowance.
- Peak: ~9k req/min (~150 rps) for ~2 hours; sustained ~50-70 rps outside spike.
- Model: multi-turn chat, median payload ~1.2k tokens; they asked to pin to an 8-bit quantized variant + prefer us-west.
- Explicit product asks from customer: temporary aggregate cap increase to 80 rps for 72 hours, routing preference to us-west, and a fallback model variant in case of capacity issues.

Product questions we need to answer in the next 6 hours so the launch team can finalize the runbook:
1) Can we support a temporary aggregated allowance of 80 rps for this account without violating other customers' SLOs? If not, what's our safe temporary cap and suggested mitigation (queuing, circuit-breaker thresholds)?
2) What product changes (pinning, routing hints, quantization variant) are required to guarantee latency under the spike, and how fast can we enact them?
3) Are there any shared resource risks (KV cache cold starts, cross-tenant batching) we should call out to the customer in the runbook?

Attachments are in the thread. I'm hoping for a quick one-page decision and a short list of action owners so I can reply to Marta with next steps.

Thanks — Grace
Director, Account Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

On Jul 15, 2028, at 09:35, Grace O'Connor wrote:
> Folks, forwarding WellHealth's traffic profile and temporary rate ask.

Thanks for the context — quick technical read and ask list below. Short answer: feasible with guardrails, but we need to coordinate routing + KV warmups and confirm the quantized variant performance.

Technical notes / risks:
- 80 rps aggregate is within our dedicated pool throughput for a small dedicated slice, but if theyre on shared hosted capacity well need to throttle other traffic unless we route them to Dedicated or apply temporary ingress isolation.
- KV cache cold starts for multi-turn flows: first 300-500 sessions during the spike may see 2-3x latency until the KV caches warm. Consider a warmup preflight (synthetic sessions) 2 hours prior to go-live.
- Quantized model pinning: we can pin to an 8-bit variant (8q) if the model is in our catalog and already benchmarked; if not, pinning will require a quick validation run (approx 4 hours) and a small rollout.
- Routing preference to us-west: we can set request routing hints; to guarantee isolation we should reserve a transient Dedicated slot for the 72-hour window. Ops changes: reserve node group, update routing policy, set temp quota override.

Action recommendations (owners):
- Karthik (me): validate 8q variant availability and run a quick 30-min perf check (ETA 3.5 hrs).
- Marcus: assess whether we can grant a temporary quota override of 80 rps on Hosted without SLA impact or if we must provision a Dedicated slice (ETA: 2 hrs for the decision + provisioning plan).
- Laura: draft the runbook notes for KV warmup and customer-facing caveats; include preflight warmup steps and rollback criteria (ETA: 1.5 hrs).

If we can't hit 80 rps safely on Hosted, propose: reserve a small Dedicated capacity and set up automated fallback to a slightly lower-latency model variant. Marcus, please include cost estimate for Dedicated reservation in your note.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Confirming our plan and immediate decisions so Grace can close the loop with WellHealth:

Decisions: 
- Temporary allowance: approved 80 rps aggregate for a 72-hour window, but we will implement it via a short-lived Dedicated reservation to avoid cross-tenant impact.
- Routing: route pilot traffic to us-west region and pin to the 8q variant. Karthik to confirm 8q perf by EOD; if 8q fails validation, we'll fallback to the verified float16 variant and reduce cap to 60 rps.
- Warmup: run synthetic warmup 2 hours before go-live (Laura to run and confirm).
- Rollback criteria: error rate >1.5% sustained for 5 minutes or median p95 latency >1200ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows -> auto-fallback to smaller model + rate reduce to 40 rps.

Action items and owners: 
- Marcus: provision Dedicated slice (small) for 72 hours, provide cost estimate and node IDs (ETA 90 mins).
- Karthik: perf validate 8q variant (ETA 3.5 hrs) and publish quick checklist in the runbook.
- Laura: complete customer-facing runbook and preflight checklist; share Drive link and short Slack summary for the on-call rotation (ETA 1.5 hrs).
- Grace: send confirmed acceptance and runbook summary to Marta and coordinate D-1 warmup window.

Ill start provisioning now and will post node details to HS-12345 when ready. Grace — you can reply to Marta with the approved plan and links.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
